governing_rules: Every 'FUN_XXX' or '0xNNNN' address anywhere in Mercs2 RE docs is keyed to ONE of these images — reference addresses by (image_id, va).
SHA-256 is the primary identity. Filenames are metadata — see aliases[] on each row.

The corpus's 'ghidra' source currently indexes ONLY v10_dump (output/_ghidra/mercs2_unpacked.exe_decomp.txt). Every other image needs its own decomp before its addresses become corpus-searchable — Phase 2 work.
The Xbox 360 devkit images (Jul 11 2008 Profile/Final) are ~6-8 weeks pre-ship — they drift from retail. Use as name/RTTI oracle only, not as address-parity oracle.
Multiple images may share the same size but different SHA-256 (mercs2_nodrm_v2, mercs2_nodrm_v3, and the retail cracked exe are all 53,482,288 B). Never key by size alone.

The PS3 asset VZ.WAD is partially encrypted (envelope 0x80800 bytes, stream cipher). Header work as of 2026-05-21 recovered an 18-byte keystream prefix; full crack is blocked on completing PS3 EBOOT RE. See wad row ps3_retail_vz_wad.
vintage_notes: The cross_platform/ analysis tree (May-June 2026) was superseded on some points: the DLC hang bisect there predates the streaming-livelock work (June 2026+) and the DLC01-is-a-level architecture. Where they conflict, later corpus work wins.
The Xenon devkits from Jul 11 2008 were widely believed close to retail early on — subsequent work confirmed real drift. Rely on them only for RTTI/string anchoring.

attempted_unblock_2026_09_07_08.outcome: all failed — attempts 1-2 unrelated (nested-analysis + pause-deadlock), attempts 3/4/5 crashed with ghidra.util.exception.ClosedException in RegisterValueStore during bulk DisassembleCommand when tocR2 painted, attempt 6 dropped tocR2 and ran for 6h 12m with 100% single-core CPU, flat working set 937 MB, no log output past initial 'opd code entries=39676 needing disasm=39676' — killed as unproductive.
attempted_unblock_2026_09_07_08.diagnosis: SeedOpdFunctions.java author's own header warned: 'disassemble() is super-linear... takes hours on ~40k entries.' Their bulk-DisassembleCommand mitigation did not scale on our 39,676-entry .opd. The engine is single-threaded internally (shared register-context AddressRangeMapDB), so adding cores does not help this specific loop.

decomp.unblock_action: Rework: (a) write a variant SeedOpd that walks .opd and calls createFunction() but SKIPS the bulk pre-disassemble — let Ghidra's downstream auto-analyzer handle disassembly across its parallel worker pool. (b) Bump MAX_CPU_CORES in tools/ghidra_12.1_PUBLIC/support/launch.properties so the decompilation-based analyzers actually use multiple cores. (c) Consider splitting into two headless runs (import + skeleton seeds with -noanalysis, then -process with analyze) so we can checkpoint.
